players.product: Carbonate fuel-cell power plants (FuelCell Energy Blocks) for behind-the-meter baseload data-center power

quarterly_data.signal: FuelCell Energy's 10-Q: as of July 31, 2026 remaining performance obligations were $263.6 million for service agreements (recognized over approximately three to fifteen years), $367.6 million for generation PPAs (approximately nineteen to twenty years) and $108.9 million for product purchase agreements (within the next two fiscal years). During the quarter the CEPA with Fit Energy added approximately $90.8 million to product purchase agreement and $110.7 million to service agreement remaining performance obligations (Phase 0).
quarterly_data.figure: RPO: service $263.6 million, generation PPAs $367.6 million, product $108.9 million; Fit Phase 0 added $90.8 million + $110.7 million

quarterly_data.signal: FuelCell Energy's 10-Q: in May 2026 FuelCell started the execution phase of expanding Torrington to accommodate an annualized production rate of 500 MW; Torrington's maximum annualized capacity under the current configuration is 100 MW per year when fully utilized. Beyond 500 MW, FuelCell has developed plans to evaluate a 'hub and spoke' model - high-volume cell manufacturing facilities and final assembly and conditioning operations at alternate locations closer to customers - targeting a potential annualized production rate of approximately 1.5 GW to 2.0 GW, with a site consultant engaged and initial site selection under way, to the extent supported by demand (no funding committed beyond the stated estimates). FuelCell says it committed capital to support these expansion plans, resulting in an increase of purchase commitments in the period: unconditional aggregate purchase commitments for materials, supplies and services were $200.6 million as of July 31, 2026, and it made significant purchase order commitments for equipment expected to be received in fiscal 2027. Annualized production rate was 35.4 MW for the nine months ended July 31, 2026 versus approximately 30.5 MW a year earlier.
quarterly_data.figure: hub-and-spoke target ~1.5-2.0 GW; purchase commitments $200.6 million; nine-month production rate 35.4 MW

quarterly_data.signal: FuelCell Energy's 10-Q: the 7.4 MW Groton Project (U.S. Navy submarine base) was not operating as of July 31, 2026 pending an upgrade of its legacy SureSource 4000 fuel cells - the only ones in FuelCell's fleet, a platform no longer sold - to three standard 2.5 MW power blocks with seven-year stack life design; a $42.6 million impairment was recorded in the nine months. Also under development: a 1.125 MW molten carbonate fuel cell system for UConn, expected to commence commercial operations in December 2027 ($4.0 million to $6.0 million of remaining investment).
quarterly_data.figure: Groton upgrade to three 2.5 MW blocks ($42.6 million impairment); UConn 1.125 MW COD December 2027

quarterly_data.signal: Customer GGE: FuelCell Energy's 10-Q - under the GGE LTSA executed on May 28, 2024, Gyeonggi Green Energy agreed to purchase 42 1.4 MW carbonate fuel cell modules to replace existing modules at its GGE Platform (21 SureSource 3000 plants), plus balance of plant replacement components and long term operations and maintenance services; the total amount payable by GGE was $159.6 million. FuelCell recognized revenue for the final 14 modules shipped to and commissioned for GGE during the nine months ended July 31, 2026.
quarterly_data.figure: GGE LTSA $159.6 million for 42 1.4 MW replacement modules

connects_to.relationship: Electricity sold to Eversource under power purchase agreements from FuelCell-owned fuel cell plants in Connecticut

contracts.signal: FuelCell Energy's 10-Q: the 7.4 MW Hartford Project, whose power will be sold to Eversource and United Illuminating over the 20-year PPA term, is now expected to complete construction and commence commercial operations by the end of calendar 2027, subject to customary development steps and financing, with approximately $34.0 million to $36.0 million of remaining investment through calendar 2027 paced by the electrical interconnection with the utility.
